pending_commit.commit_message: nebraska: Use signal handlers instead of waiting for input Use signals instead of input for properly exiting the server. The previous approach would fail when a remote SSH connection kills the nebraska. Users running locally can easily do CTRL + C to kill the process. BUG=chromium:920404 TEST=unitests TEST=./nebraska.py Change-Id: I759a85b84d2525098e506a799cfb2a32c1c74745 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1518801 Commit-Ready: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Tested-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Xiaochu Liu <xiaochu@chromium.org>

nebraska: Change --{update|install}-payloads flags Change --update-payloads to --update-metadata to accurately describe what the directory is. We only look for the payload.json files in this directory and we don't care where the actual payloads are located. The payloads themselves are located/served by --payload-address. -- Same above change for install-payloads (-> install-metadata) BUG=chromium:920404 TEST=unittest TEST=./nebraska.py Change-Id: I074ca520938d0ad76ee45336cb243860e0e92344 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1518802 Commit-Ready: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Tested-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org>

nebraska: Break --payload-addr into two flags Currently, the nebraska adds /update or /install to the --payload-addr flag based on whether the request is install or update. But this is unfair to the server/service that serves the payload. They have to change their code semantics in order to handle this. Even more complicated we send an Omaha request to a devserver address like: "http://devserver-address/update" so the devserver so can send a response back. Now adding /update or /install to the end of addresses like this can become more confusing and cumbersome. So instead of nebraska making such assumptions, we should directly pass the addresses for install and updates to nebraska. If no address for install was passed we use the update address instead. So flag --payload-addr was replaced by two flags --update-payloads-address and --install-payloads-address. BUG=chromium:920404 TEST=unittest TEST=./nebraska.py Change-Id: Iaebc3e78a4d80f7085464c87b62622d7129ea66b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1518803 Commit-Ready: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Tested-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Norvez <norvez@chromium.org>

dependency: fix bug that causes dependency source paths to be incorrect Currently, many sources paths in the resulted json deps file are prefixed with the directory which the build_api script is invoked with. e.g: "/mnt/host/source/src/third_party/chromiumos-overlay/eclass" This is because of a bug in how source paths are handled in dependency. After the source paths, they are converted to relative paths with respect to CHROOT_SOURCE_ROOT. Then to filter out paths that are subdirectories of others, they are converted to absolute path again using os.path.abspath(..), but this instead uses the current directory script is invoked with as the root directory. This CLs fixes the problem by not converting source paths to relative path before filtering out subdirectories. It also add check in NormalizeSourcePaths() method to ensure that all the input paths are absolute paths. TEST=run `./bin/build_api chromite.api.DependencyService/GetBuildDependencyGraph --input-json=input.json --output-json=output.json` and verify all the source paths look correct BUG=chromium:938605 Change-Id: Ibd0ed9587c9e6dbce7773a4b47c869beecb67eff Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1525869 Commit-Ready: Ned Nguyen <nednguyen@google.com> Tested-by: Ned Nguyen <nednguyen@google.com> Reviewed-by: Ned Nguyen <nednguyen@google.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Abraham <seanabraham@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Alex Klein <saklein@chromium.org>

diagnostics: add status_message field to GetRoutineUpdateResponse. GetRoutineUpdateResponse has a single field, output, which holds both the result of a routine, e.g. "Failed to start the urandom executable" as well as any accumulated logs. Add a new field to GetRoutineUpdateResponse, status_message, to hold the result of a routine, and let output be only the accumulated logs. This allows for a routine like battery_sysfs to separate the log messages from a detailed status message. shill: wifi: Examine assoc/auth status codes at disconnect CL:1226113 uses 802.11 disconnect reasons to generate more suitable shill disconnect reasons. However, assoc/auth status codes are still not used. Of particular importance is when a connection fails due to a pending timeout, as supplicant will always see this as a user disconnect (reason 3). Looking at the assoc/auth status codes provides us with more information, allowing for more accurate shill disconnect reasons. This change also uploads the status codes of assoc/auth failures to UMA. BUG=chromium:625387 TEST=-All unit tests are passing. -Set up AP unable to accept more STAs, and ensured that Shill returned a "too-many-stas" error through its external DBus interface. Change-Id: I4fbcb4aaaf5dbdf0ec7b7e7560e4a9d7225cc2e0 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1487575 Commit-Ready: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Tested-by: Alex Khouderchah <akhouderchah@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Eric Caruso <ejcaruso@chromium.org>
